To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human islets and inflammatory dendritic cells can generate deamidated, HLA‐DQB1‐restricted islet autoantigen peptides.
deamidation can be induced in pancreatic islets and dendritc cells, and that deamidated peptides are presented by the highest‐risk HLA class II molecules in the presence of native peptides.

(i) deamidated human islet autoantigen peptides are naturally processed and presented by human dendritic cells, (ii) deamidation occurs in human pancreatic islets in response to inflammatory stimuli and (iii) deamidating enzyme activity is present in human pancreatic islet cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterisation of deamidation as an important mechanism in T1D pathogenesis and the development of a novel vaccine approach to prevent T1D.
the role of deamidation in T1D and provides a new insight into the mechanisms of neoepitope generation in T1D.
the role of post‐translitional modification of islet proteins and their presentation to T cells in the development of type 1 Diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deamidation process may play a significant role in the initiation or exacerbation of type 1 Diabetes.
deamidated epitopes are present in human pancreas and can be processed and presented by DC to T cells.
the data presented herein indicate that deamidated peptides can be generated in human islets and that deamidation can be induced by inflammatory cytokines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
deamidation occurs in human islets, inflammatory DC and tolDC.

deamidation can occur on insulin and other islet autoantigen proteins in both pancreatic islets and dendritc cells, that this process is increased in an inflammatory environment and that deamidated peptides can be presented by the highest risk HLA molecules.

the inflammatory microenvironment in the islets of Langerhans and in the pancreatic lymph nodes may be a source of post‐translationally modified islet auto‐antigens, such as deamidated epitopes of insulin, that may initiate the T1D autoimmune response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inflammatory environment in the pancreas may contribute to neoepitope generation and that deamidated peptides are presented by DC to T cells.
the deamidation pathway can be activated in islet‐derived cells and that this may be a potential mechanism by which neoepitopes are presented to T cells in T1D.
islets and DC are both sources of deamitaded neoepitope autoantigens that may play a role in T1D pathogenesis.
